question: What survives when the public Hessdalen record is split into event occurrence, sensor channel, common-cause inference and extraordinary interpretation?

evidence_findings.finding: The 1984 project preserved a structured technical report with instruments, event summaries and appendices rather than only later folklore.
evidence_findings.effect: G1_EVENT_OCCURRENCE has source-bound historical support for multiple reported events.

evidence_findings.finding: The 1984 report states that its F/G classification was subjective and notes that only six reports had F9 or higher, with four of those also G7 or higher; the author explicitly says this was too little to draw conclusions about the nature of the light or common properties.
evidence_findings.effect: Historical high-anomaly labels cannot be treated as objective ground truth or as evidence that all reports belong to one phenomenon.

evidence_findings.finding: The 1984 report lists 36 radar recordings; only three were also visually observed as lights. The report also states that many radar-only returns were not photographed as unusual objects and that continuous radar/spectrum monitoring was not achieved.
evidence_findings.effect: At least limited multi-channel overlap is documented, but sensor independence and common-cause identity remain unproven.

evidence_findings.finding: For 1984-01-27 22:58 local project time, the report gives two radar echoes about 2.4 seconds apart and roughly 20–21 km separated, yielding a reported minimum speed near 8.5 km/s; visual observers separately reported a fast south-to-north light around the same event window.
evidence_findings.effect: This is a high-value historical event for reconstruction, but the archived report is not equivalent to surviving raw radar video, calibration replay or independent range confirmation.

evidence_findings.finding: The report notes four of ten F5-or-higher light registrations during a limited interval occurred near magnetic pulsations, while also warning that many pulsations occurred during those days and coincidence was possible.
evidence_findings.effect: No causal magnetic link is promoted.

evidence_findings.finding: The 1984 report found no useful contemporaneous result from Geiger counter, seismograph or IR viewer in the limited observations described, and explicitly treated the IR sample as too small for a conclusion.
evidence_findings.effect: Negative and low-power channels are preserved rather than omitted.

evidence_findings.finding: Current Project Hessdalen documentation says two 4K cameras record continuously, 20-minute video segments are stacked, public stacks have been available since September 2024, original videos exist from November 2024 and selected/full-day raw video is made available for testing.
evidence_findings.effect: A modern independent replay route exists in principle.

evidence_findings.finding: The current project documentation explicitly lists stars, satellites, birds, insects, planes, h264 compression shadows, moon/sun lens reflections and other artifacts as things visible in stacked products.
evidence_findings.effect: Any stack-only anomaly must pass an artifact and known-object attack before promotion.

killer_tests_next.test: Select one full public raw-video day before inspecting anomaly labels; freeze camera geometry and detection thresholds; independently classify all tracks against stars, satellites, meteors, aircraft, birds/insects and optical/compression artifacts.

For candidate events visible on separated cameras, solve line-of-sight geometry with clock uncertainty and require a physically consistent distance/trajectory before assigning speed or local-atmosphere origin.
Require synchronized raw timestamps across optical plus at least one independent non-optical channel; publish clock error bounds and false-trigger behavior.

Reconstruct the 1984-01-27 22:58 radar/visual event from the appendix geometry, radar specifications, sweep cadence and uncertainty; test ground-clutter, propagation, aircraft and timing alternatives before treating the reported ~8.5 km/s as physical motion.
Build mundane controls on one date range, freeze classification rules, then score an independent holdout range. Only residuals that survive the frozen rules enter the anomaly queue.

compact_result: HUNT-0001 does not start by declaring the Hessdalen Lights one object or one phenomenon. The public record supports a real, long-running corpus of recurrent reports and some instrument-channel overlap, but the 1984 project itself documented subjective classification, sparse high-quality/high-anomaly cases, limited visual-radar overlap, incomplete continuous monitoring and ambiguous magnetic correlation. Modern data availability makes Hessdalen unusually suitable for a stronger replay. TOPA therefore promotes the site to REPLICATION_WORTHY while refusing extraordinary or single-common-cause promotion.
